title: Scripture and the Church
definition: Scripture and the Church means God’s Word forms, governs, corrects, nourishes, and sends the people of Christ.
summary: Scripture and the Church means God’s Word forms, governs, corrects, nourishes, and sends the people of Christ.
christFocus: Jesus is the head of the Church, and Scripture teaches His people how to gather, worship, serve, love, restore, and live on mission.

studySections.heading: Doctrine in Summary
studySections.content:
The Church is not created by human preference, programs, or personalities. Christ gathers His people, and Scripture teaches the Church what it is and how it should live.

God’s Word nourishes the Church through teaching, preaching, correction, worship, prayer, ordinances, fellowship, and mission. When Scripture is central, the Church is protected from drifting into entertainment, control, division, or shallow religion.

Jesus is the head of the Church. Scripture and the Church reminds believers that no pastor, tradition, trend, or ministry owns Christ’s people. The Church belongs to Him.

studySections.heading: Why This Matters
studySections.content:
People wounded by church may struggle to trust Christian community again. Scripture helps distinguish Christ’s design for His Church from the failures and sins of people who misuse His name.

This doctrine also challenges isolated believers. Christ saves individuals into a people who need truth, love, accountability, service, and shared worship.

studySections.heading: Discipleship and Application
studySections.content: Let Scripture shape your understanding of church rather than pain, preference, or culture alone. Seek Christ-centered fellowship, serve with humility, receive correction, and help build a community where God’s Word leads and Christ is honored.
